title: AI Voice Agent Services: A Smarter Way to Automate Business Communication
description:
Think about how many times customers contact a business just to ask a simple question, check an appointment, or get an update. Handling every interaction manually can take up valuable employee time, particularly when a company receives a large number of calls each day.

Modern businesses are finding new ways to manage these conversations without compromising customer experience. One technology gaining attention is AI voice agent services.

AI voice agents allow people to communicate with software using everyday spoken language. Instead of following fixed phone instructions, customers can explain what they need, ask follow-up questions, and receive relevant responses. This creates opportunities for businesses to simplify communication while making their services more accessible.

Let's explore how voice AI works, where businesses can use it, and what it takes to develop an effective voice-powered solution.

What Makes an AI Voice Agent Useful for Businesses?

An AI voice agent is a software-based assistant that communicates with users through speech. It combines different artificial intelligence technologies to understand spoken requests and respond appropriately.

Traditional automated calling systems usually depend on numbered menus. Customers may have to listen to several options before finding the right department. AI voice agents take a different approach by allowing users to describe their requirements naturally.

For instance, someone calling an automobile dealership might say, "I want to book a service appointment for Friday." The voice agent can understand the request and, when connected to the dealership's scheduling system, help identify available appointments.

Several technologies work together to make this possible:

Automatic Speech Recognition: Converts a person's speech into text.

Natural Language Understanding: Identifies the meaning and purpose behind a request.

AI Language Models: Help generate responses based on the conversation and available information.

Text-to-Speech Technology: Turns generated responses into spoken language.

System Integrations: Connect the voice assistant with business tools and applications.

The result is a communication experience that can adapt to different questions instead of depending entirely on predefined commands.

Five Ways AI Voice Agents Can Improve Business Operations

Introducing voice automation can help businesses manage everyday communication more effectively. Its value becomes clearer when applied to specific operational challenges.

1. Making Customer Assistance More Accessible

Customers should not have to wait for an available representative just to receive basic information.

An AI voice agent can respond to common questions about services, opening hours, pricing information, and business procedures. This gives customers another convenient way to find answers.

Human employees can then concentrate on requests that require detailed explanations or individual attention.

2. Managing Calls Outside Business Hours

Many businesses receive inquiries when their offices are closed. Missing these conversations can mean losing potential customers or delaying important requests.

Depending on its configuration, an AI voice agent can continue handling routine interactions during evenings, weekends, and holidays.

A customer might request business information, leave details for a callback, or arrange an appointment without waiting until the next working day.

3. Supporting Sales Conversations

Voice automation is not limited to customer service. It can also assist businesses with their initial sales interactions.

For example, a digital marketing agency could use an AI voice agent to ask prospective clients about their business goals, marketing requirements, and preferred consultation times.

The collected information can be shared with the sales team so that employees have a better understanding of the inquiry before following up.

4. Handling Repetitive Administrative Requests

Some business conversations follow predictable patterns. Appointment confirmations, basic service questions, and routine information requests are common examples.

Automating suitable interactions can reduce repetitive work and give employees more time for activities that require problem-solving and personal judgment.

5. Creating More Consistent Interactions

Businesses want customers to receive accurate information regardless of when they call or which department they contact.

An AI voice agent connected to an approved business knowledge base can provide consistent answers to frequently asked questions.

Companies must still review the information regularly and establish clear procedures for handling uncertain or sensitive requests.

How to Build an AI Voice Agent That Meets Business Needs

Knowing how to build an AI voice agent starts with understanding the problem it should solve. Selecting technology before defining the purpose can result in a system that sounds impressive but offers little practical value.

Here is a more useful development approach.

Step 1: Decide What the Agent Should Handle

Identify the conversations that consume the most time in your business. These might include appointment requests, product inquiries, customer support, or initial sales discussions.

Choose one clear use case before expanding into additional functions.

Step 2: Find a Suitable Conversational AI Platform

A conversational AI platform provides the underlying capabilities needed to understand requests and manage spoken interactions.

Evaluate its language support, integration options, customization features, response quality, security, and ability to handle increasing usage.

Step 3: Give the System Reliable Business Information

An AI agent needs trustworthy information to respond accurately.

Prepare relevant company documents, product details, service information, policies, and frequently asked questions. Make sure the content is organized and updated when business information changes.

Step 4: Design Conversations Around People

This is where Voice First Design becomes especially important.

People do not always speak in perfectly structured sentences. They may change their minds, interrupt a response, provide incomplete information, or ask an unrelated question.

A well-designed voice experience should handle these situations gracefully. It should ask for clarification when necessary and make human assistance available when the conversation becomes too complicated.

Step 5: Connect the Agent With Existing Tools

A voice assistant becomes more useful when it can interact with the systems a business already uses.

Integrations with CRM software, appointment calendars, customer databases, and support applications can help the agent retrieve information and complete authorized tasks.

Step 6: Evaluate Real Conversations

Before making the system available to customers, test it with different accents, speaking styles, questions, and unexpected situations.

Review where misunderstandings occur and improve the conversation flow. Continue monitoring performance after launch rather than treating development as a one-time activity.

Why Voice Application Development Requires a Thoughtful Approach

Building a voice-enabled product involves more than connecting speech recognition with an AI model.

Professional Voice Application Development brings together software architecture, conversational logic, speech technologies, integrations, and user experience.

For example, an appointment-booking voice application must understand dates, confirm customer details, check availability, and communicate booking results correctly. Each step needs to work together.

Voice First Design adds another important dimension by placing spoken interaction at the center of the experience rather than treating it as an additional feature.

This approach helps businesses create applications that are easier to interact with and better suited to real customer needs.

Where Can Businesses Apply Voice AI?

Different industries can use voice automation to address their communication requirements.

Healthcare: Managing appointment requests, reminders, and general administrative questions.

Real Estate: Collecting property preferences and arranging meetings with agents.

Retail: Answering product questions and providing order-related information.

Financial Services: Supporting general inquiries and directing customers to appropriate departments.

Travel and Hospitality: Handling reservation questions and providing information about available services.

Each application should include suitable privacy protections, access controls, and escalation procedures, particularly when handling personal or financial information.

Voice Technology and the Next Generation of Digital Experiences

The way people interact with software is gradually expanding beyond traditional screens, buttons, and menus. Voice offers another way to access information and complete everyday tasks.

As AI technology advances, voice applications may become better at understanding conversational context, managing connected workflows, and adapting responses to individual situations.

This shift is closely connected to the ideas behind Voice First.

At Voice First, Howard Tiersky explores how software can be designed around natural human conversation. The project looks beyond automated phone calls and considers how voice can become a primary interface for interacting with digital products and services.

For business owners, developers, and digital product teams, understanding this approach can open up new possibilities for building more natural software experiences.

Conclusion

AI voice agent services are giving businesses a new way to approach customer communication. They can help manage routine calls, support sales activities, improve access to information, and reduce repetitive administrative work.

However, the real value comes from building solutions around actual customer needs. A useful AI voice agent requires reliable information, thoughtful conversation design, appropriate integrations, and a clear way to involve human employees when necessary.

Through Voice Application Development, Voice First Design, and conversational AI innovation, businesses can explore communication experiences that feel more natural and practical.

title: How we tell parents what a teen's AI chat was about, without showing them the chat
description:
Most parental controls for teens were built around one idea: let the parent see everything. Every text, every search, every message. That design breaks down with AI chatbots.

Teens talk to ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Character.AI about things they won't say out loud to anyone. Stress, friendships, their bodies, their sexuality, whether they're okay. If a parent can read those chats word for word, two things happen fast. The teen finds out, and the teen moves to an app the parent doesn't know about.

When we built TeenCue, we started from a different question: what is the least a parent needs to know to make a good decision? Our answer was the topic and how concerning it is. Not the words.

This post walks through how that works.

The output: topic and concern level, nothing else

For every message a teen sends on a supported AI chat service, TeenCue produces a small record:

  • Service: which AI it was (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Character.AI, Copilot and so on)
  • Category and topic: what the message was about, at a level like "school", "emotional support" or "relationships"
  • Concern level: how likely it is that a parent should check in

That record is what the parent sees in the dashboard, the iPhone app and the weekly Teen Brief email. Parents never see what was typed.

A typical brief reads something like: TeenCue noticed 1 signal that may be worth a conversation. It was related to leaning on AI for emotional support. That is enough for a parent to know it's time to talk, and it leaves the teen's words with the teen.

Rating the message

To produce that record, the message has to be read by something. We use an AI rating model from Anthropic, the company behind Claude.

The flow is short:

  1. The teen sends a message to an AI chat service in their browser or in Safari on their iPhone.
  2. TeenCue sends that message securely to the rating model with a prompt that asks for one thing: a structured rating (category, topic, concern level), not a summary and not a quote.
  3. TeenCue stores the rating and discards the message text.

Asking for a structured rating instead of free text matters. A summary is just the chat in shorter form. A topic plus a level is something a parent can act on without learning what their kid actually said.

What we keep and what we don't

We keep:

  • The rating (service, category, topic, concern level)
  • Counts and timing, so a parent can see things like "24 AI chats across 3 services this week"

We don't keep:

  • The text the teen typed
  • The AI's replies
  • Other websites or browsing history

We're also upfront about the one place text does exist briefly. Anthropic, the rating provider, deletes the message within 30 days, except for chats its own systems flag for safety, which it can keep for up to 2 years. That is Anthropic's retention policy, and we'd rather say it plainly than hide it behind "never stored."

Ratings can be wrong

A model rating a single message without context will sometimes get it wrong. "I want to die" means something very different after a math test than it does at 2am.

So TeenCue treats a rating as a reason to talk, not a verdict. The product language is deliberately soft ("may be worth a look") and the parent view shows patterns across a week, not a single alarming line. The goal is a calm conversation, not a confrontation built on one flagged message.

Designed to be used openly

TeenCue does nothing until it's paired with a parent account using a short code, and we tell parents to let their teen know it's installed. That's not just ethics. Monitoring that relies on secrecy fails the moment it's discovered, and teens always discover it. Monitoring a teen knows about, and that doesn't expose their words, is something they can live with.

Where it runs

  • iPhone: Apple's Screen Time APIs plus a Safari extension, no VPN or MDM. We wrote about that in How we keep AI chatbots inside Safari on a teen's iPhone.
  • Computers: an extension for Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Brave.

If you're a parent, you can try it free for a week at teencue.com. If you're an engineer working on privacy-preserving safety tools, we'd like to hear how you'd approach this differently.

title: Turn any website into clean Markdown for RAG without a headless browser
description:
If you've built a RAG chatbot, you know the boring part is getting clean text out of websites. Navigation menus, cookie banners, footers and "related posts" widgets all end up in your embeddings and hurt retrieval.

The common answer is "spin up a headless browser and crawl." That works, but it's slow and memory-hungry, and on most hosted platforms it's billed by compute time, so you can't predict the cost.

Most docs sites, blogs and help centers don't need a browser at all: the content is already in the HTML. So I built a crawler that skips the browser entirely.

What it does

Website to Markdown for LLM & RAG is an Apify actor that:

  • crawls from your start URLs and stays on the same domain, with optional sitemap.xml discovery
  • extracts only the main content (headings, lists, code blocks and tables) as Markdown
  • can chunk pages for embeddings, with overlap; you pay per page, not per chunk
  • respects robots.txt and supports include/exclude URL patterns
  • returns title, description, author, date, language and word count for each page

Benchmark: HTTP vs headless Chromium

Same 30 pages, 5 parallel requests, Playwright Chromium vs plain HTTP plus extraction:

Site HTTP (this actor) Headless browser Speed-up
MDN Web Docs 1.0 s 9.5 s 9.8x
MDN Web Docs (cold) 3.2 s 8.1 s 2.5x
Simple static blog 1.9 s 3.4 s 1.8x
Heavy news site finished timed out –

The heavier the page (scripts, ads, trackers), the bigger the gap. Price is flat: $1 per 1,000 pages, plus $0.01 per run.

Use it from Python 

from apify_client import ApifyClient

client = ApifyClient("YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN")
run = client.actor("datacraft-tools/web-to-markdown").call(run_input={
    "startUrls": [{"url": "https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/"}],
    "maxPages": 100,
    "maxCrawlDepth": 2,
    "chunkSize": 2000,
    "chunkOverlap": 200,
})

for item in client.dataset(run["defaultDatasetId"]).iterate_items():
    print(item["url"], item["chunkIndex"], item["markdown"][:80])

Each row is ready to embed. Push markdown into Pinecone, Qdrant, Chroma or pgvector together with url and title as metadata.

When NOT to use it

If a site renders its content only with JavaScript (some single-page apps), an HTTP crawler will see an empty page and you need a browser-based crawler. For docs, blogs, news, marketing sites and knowledge bases, HTTP is the faster and cheaper choice.

I built this actor. Feedback and feature requests are welcome in the comments.

title: PII masking at the LLM gateway: log the redaction, not the PII
description:
If you put an LLM gateway in front of your models, sooner or later someone pastes a customer record into a prompt. Masking it is the easy part. The harder question is what you write to your own logs.

A common mistake is to keep the original prompt "for audit". Then your audit log holds the exact personal data you wanted to protect.

This is how we handle it in BaseLLM, the self-hosted AI gateway we build at Base Interactive.

Scan before the request leaves the network

The gateway scans the text before it reaches the model. Detection is rule based and runs on the server, so the text is not sent to another service for checking. Settings are per project.

There are five modes:

  • Report only: the request goes through and the detection is logged
  • Mask: TCKN 100*****46, ***4567
  • Placeholder: the model sees <TELEFON_1>, the real value is put back in the answer
  • Redact: [REDACTED:TC_KIMLIK]
  • Block: 403 pii_blocked, the request never reaches the model

Secrets (API keys, tokens, connection strings) have their own 29 rules and are blocked by default with 403 secret_blocked.

Check digits matter

Regex alone masks too much. An 11 digit order number looks like a Turkish ID number. So we validate check digits for Turkish ID and tax numbers, IBANs, license plates, and Luhn for cards. In our own test set of 22 realistic samples, 20 were detected with no false positives. Names and addresses can't be found with patterns, so they are out of scope (you can add your own patterns).

What goes to the log

  • The raw value is never stored
  • Only the masked sample, counters and where it was found
  • Every detection is an audit event (pii.detection), and audit records are linked with a SHA-256 chain so a changed record is visible
  • Detection events are kept 90 days by default, configurable from 0 to 3650 days

So the log proves the masking happened, without becoming a second copy of the data.

Masking is one technical measure, not full compliance by itself. But it is the part security teams ask about first.

Details: https://llm.baseinteractive.com.tr/en/docs/data-masking

title: RAG gives confident wrong answers: what actually fixes it
description:
Most RAG hallucination is a retrieval failure, not a model failure. Here is where it breaks and what fixes it.
tags: ai, machinelearning, llm, beginners
canonical_url: https://community.oneshopai.com/posts/rag-gives-confident-wrong-answers-what-actually-fixes-it-8a8c0d2a-704b-41b5-a652-0999472877d9
cover_image:

If you are new to this: RAG just means the AI looks things up in your documents before answering, instead of answering from memory. Most of what goes wrong is in the looking up, not the answering.

We have been building a RAG assistant on our own docs, and it keeps hitting the failure everyone hits. It passes testing, then starts giving confident wrong answers. Here is what is actually going on underneath.

Why does RAG give wrong answers?

Almost never the model. If the retrieved chunks do not contain the answer, the model fills the gap, and it fills it fluently. Most of what gets called hallucination is a retrieval problem wearing a costume.

Before blaming generation, log what was actually retrieved for the question that failed. Nine times out of ten the answer was not in there.

How should you chunk documents for RAG?

Fixed-size splitting is the default and it is the first thing to change. Cutting every 500 or 1000 tokens slices tables in half and separates a heading from the text beneath it, so the model answers from fragments that lost their context.

Chunk on document structure instead: split at headings, keep sections whole, and carry the heading text into the chunk so the retriever knows what the section is about.

Hybrid search vs vector search: which one for RAG?

Pure vector search misses exact strings. Product names, error codes, version numbers.

Embeddings match meaning, not characters, so someone searching an exact term can get back everything except the page containing it. Run keyword search alongside the vector search and merge the results. If your users type exact terms, you need both.

How do you stop RAG from hallucinating?

Two rules do most of the work.

Require the model to quote the chunk it used, so an unsupported answer becomes visible instead of invisible. And set a confidence threshold: if nothing retrieved scores above it, the answer is "this is not in the docs" rather than a guess.

Refusals go up, wrong answers drop much further. A refusal is a cheaper failure than a confident lie.

How do you evaluate a RAG system?

Write real questions with known answers and run them on every change. Without that you are going on "feels better", which is not a measurement, and you will not catch the change that quietly made retrieval worse.

No framework needed to start. A spreadsheet with a question column and an expected answer column is enough.

The one still unsolved: multi-document questions

Questions needing two documents at once still break it. It retrieves from one and answers as though that is the whole picture, confidently, which is the worst combination.

What is the worst wrong answer yours has given?

Paste it in the comments. The failures are more useful than the fixes, and I would rather we collect them in one place than everyone hit the same ones separately.

Originally posted on the OneShopAI Community

title: Cloudflare Worker dead-man switch on the free plan: the cron didn't fire
description:
Everything I've got that watches my homelab lives in my homelab. Uptime Kuma, my agents, the little ESP32 watchdog board. That's fine until the power goes or the internet drops. Then all of it goes quiet at the same moment, and quiet is exactly what "everything's fine" looks like from my phone.

So on 13 October 2026 I built a dead-man switch that lives somewhere else. My boxes check in every minute. If the check-ins stop, something off-site notices and posts to Discord. It runs on Cloudflare's free plan.

How it's put together

  • Senders: both my Proxmox nodes run a systemd timer that does a curl POST every 60 seconds. Since 16 October my ESP32 watchdog board pings it too, every check cycle.
  • The Worker checks a secret path segment and a bearer token. If either is wrong it returns a plain 404, so from outside it looks like nothing's there. It also 404s any check name it doesn't know, so a typo can't quietly create a new check.
  • A Durable Object holds the state: one SQLite row per check, with last seen time and up/down state.
  • The grace period is 300 seconds per check.
  • Discord messages: ⚠️ when a check stops, ✅ when it comes back (with how long it was silent), and 🚨 "Home offline?" if every check goes down at once. That last one is the power cut or internet case.

Why a Durable Object and not KV

Honestly, because of my API token. The Cloudflare token I deploy with can edit Worker scripts but can't do KV or D1. A SQLite-backed Durable Object only needs the scripts permission, so it just worked. It's also a better fit: one object, one small table, and state changes happen in one place.

Usage is tiny. About 4.5k requests a day against the free plan's 100k.

The bit that didn't work: the cron never fired

My first version was the obvious design. Worker for check-ins, plus a cron trigger (* * * * *) that runs every minute and sweeps for anything that's gone quiet too long.

First test, I paused the pings from one node. It went silent for 414 seconds, well past the 300 second grace. No alert.

I looked at the Worker's invocations through Cloudflare's GraphQL analytics. There were check-in invocations and nothing else. The scheduled handler hadn't run at all. For the first 10 minutes or so after deploying, the cron trigger simply didn't fire.

I don't know why, and I didn't need to. What it told me was more useful: if a dead-man switch's own timer can just not run, then the switch is only as good as that timer. And a cron trigger isn't something I can see or test properly from my side.

The fix: the object wakes itself up

Durable Objects have alarms. You set a time, and the object's alarm() method gets called then. So now the object keeps its own clock:

// Self-rearming 60 s alarm: the sweep keeps running even when every check-in has stopped.
// The cron trigger is only a backup that re-creates the alarm if it was ever lost.
async arm() {
  if ((await this.ctx.storage.getAlarm()) === null) await this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + 60000);
}

async alarm() {
  await this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + 60000);
  await this.sweep();
}

Every ping and every sweep calls arm(), so there's always an alarm set. The alarm handler sets the next one first, then sweeps. The cron trigger is still there, but now it's just a backup. All it does is call the sweep, and the sweep re-arms the alarm if it ever went missing.

Two other small things in the code I'm glad I did:

  • A check that has never been seen still alerts. On its first sweep a new check gets its clock started, so if it never arrives at all, it goes down after the grace period like anything else.
  • The secret comparisons are constant-time. Probably overkill for a homelab, but it's six lines.

Testing it properly this time

I paused the same node's pings again. The ⚠️ alert came at about 6 minutes, which is what you'd expect from a 5 minute grace and a sweep every minute. When I let the pings resume, the ✅ recovery message arrived 4 seconds later, because recovery is handled on the ping itself, not on the next sweep.

Here's what the switch thinks right now, from my deploy script's status command:

One nice side effect of using a webhook

On 16 October I wanted these alerts in a different Discord channel. A webhook's channel can be changed with a PATCH, and the webhook URL stays the same. So I moved it without touching the Worker at all. No redeploy.

What I'd do differently

  • Don't trust a scheduler you can't watch. If the whole point is "notice when nothing happens", the thing doing the noticing needs its own heartbeat. The alarm gives me that.
  • Test the silence, not the noise. My first test was the right one: stop a sender and wait. It's the only test that matters for a dead-man switch.
  • Make the "everything is down" message different. One box going quiet and the whole house going quiet are different problems. The 🚨 message tells me which one it is before I've even opened anything.
  • Keep it boring. No dependencies, one Worker file, about 120 lines.

I wrote about the ESP32 watchdog board separately. Between the two, the board tells me when a service is down, and this tells me when the board can't.

What do you use for the "the whole house is offline" case? I'd love to know if anyone's doing it a simpler way.

🤖 Drafted with AI assistance from my own homelab notes, logs and repos, and fact-checked against them before publishing.

title: SWE-sweep: a benchmark that makes coding agents find the bugs themselves
description:
SWE-sweep

Most coding benchmarks hand the agent a bug report and ask for a fix. Real work does not. SWE-sweep, from Meta researchers including two of the creators of SWE-bench, gives a coding agent a real repository and no hint about what is broken, where it is, or what kind of bug it is. The agent has to find the bugs and repair them. Across 4,068 known bugs in 100 repositories and 22 languages, the best model tested fixed only 4.7 percent, verified by hidden tests. Discovery, not repair, is the hard part. If you build coding agents, this is the benchmark to watch, and the one to run your own agent against.

What you get

  • A benchmark for teams building coding agents who want to measure discovery, not just repair
  • A score for how many bugs an agent can find and fix in large codebases, verified by hidden tests
  • A paper and site at swesweep.com, published 1 October 2026, with the full results
  • A live repo with 246 stars, no release yet, and no stated licence

Do not trust a benchmark that hands the agent the bug report. Run your agent against SWE-sweep and see whether it can find the bug before it fixes it.

Repo: https://github.com/facebookresearch/swe-sweep

Quick poll

What would you use SWE-sweep for first?

  • Running my own agent against it
  • Reading the paper first
  • Comparing models on it
  • Watching it for now

Vote in the comments.

If you found SWE-sweep interesting, I write about tools like this every week in The AI-Native Engineering Leader, what actually works for engineering leaders building with AI agents, and what to skip.

title: Apple’s Next AI Could Take Over the Mac
description:
Quick take

  • Apple’s job listing describes a general-purpose computer-use agent that could browse the web, run commands, write and debug code, and call APIs.
  • TechCrunch reported the project appears to be in its early stages, with a possible release as soon as late 2027, though Apple has not confirmed it.
  • Apple said macOS would add stronger Full Disk Access controls and require more explicit user action for sensitive-data access, citing autonomous AI risks.
  • Apple would enter a competitive field involving OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google, which has begun rolling out similar Mac functionality through Gemini.

Why it matters

For Mac users and developers, Apple’s plans point to a shift from separate apps and broad, conventional permissions toward an operating system where an Apple agent could coordinate work under tightly managed access. Third-party agents may face stricter barriers, while users will need to watch whether Apple delivers the project and makes its actions predictable, visible and reversible.

Imagine asking your Mac to research a trip, compare prices, update a spreadsheet, test a script and send the results by email. Apple appears to be exploring an agent that could handle that entire chain of work, moving between apps and services as a human operator would.

Apple’s job listing for a senior engineering manager describes a general-purpose computer-use agent that can browse the web, work across applications, run commands, write and debug code, call services through APIs and complete multi-step tasks.

Aerial view of Apple Park dllu · Daniel L. Lu (user:dllu) · via wikipedia · CC BY-SA 4.0

The listing presents an AI system that would not simply answer questions inside a chat window. It would decide which tool to use at each stage of a job, shifting between a browser, a desktop application, a command line, source code and online services. In practical terms, that could mean turning a broad request into a sequence of actions performed across the Mac.

The system is described as needing privacy and safety controls, suggesting that Apple sees computer control as both a product opportunity and a permissions challenge. An agent that can read files, operate software and execute commands would need a much wider range of access than a conventional assistant.

TechCrunch reported that the work appears to be in its early stages. The report, based on Apple job listings, said Apple could be aiming for a release as soon as late 2027, although that timetable is uncertain and the company has not confirmed the project.

If Apple completes the system, the Mac could become less like a collection of separate applications and more like a single workspace directed through intent. A user might describe an outcome rather than open each program manually. The agent could gather information in Safari, place it in a document, run a data analysis script and prepare a message without requiring the user to coordinate every transition.

That vision places Apple in a market where other companies are already pursuing computer-operating agents. TechCrunch’s report pointed to efforts from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta, while Google has begun rolling out similar functionality for Macs through Gemini. Apple would therefore be entering an increasingly competitive field rather than defining it alone.

The company’s distinctive problem is control. Apple has long made privacy and platform security central to its product strategy, but an agent cannot be useful if it is prevented from seeing the information or operating the applications needed to complete a task. The more capable the agent becomes, the more its permissions begin to resemble those of a human administrator.

Apple’s own platform changes show that tension developing. In its announcement on updates to Full Disk Access, Apple said macOS would add stronger controls and require more explicit user action for access to sensitive data. The company cited the growing risks created by increasingly capable and autonomous AI agents.

Those changes could make it harder for third-party agents to obtain broad control of a Mac while Apple develops an agent intended to work deeply across the operating system. A future Apple assistant might receive carefully designed privileges unavailable to outside developers, raising questions about competition as well as security.

The risks are not theoretical. The Associated Press reported on privacy concerns surrounding AI agents, including an incident in which an agent disclosed a user’s home address and made other unexpected decisions. Georgia Tech cybersecurity professor Veronica Rivera compared such systems to giving someone keys and a to-do list. The metaphor captures the central issue: an agent may understand the assignment while still making consequential choices along the way.

There has also been criticism of Apple’s permission design. MacRumors reported that forum user waydabber considered the new warnings and persistent transparency indicators confusing and intrusive for developers, while acknowledging the security rationale. The reactions cited here are cautionary. No comparable supportive response was identified in the provided coverage.

Apple will ultimately need to make computer control feel predictable, visible and reversible. Users may welcome an assistant that removes tedious work, but they will also need to know what it can see, which actions it took and how to stop it when a routine task begins to drift. The Mac’s next interface may be conversational, but trust will determine whether people allow it to act.

Sources

  • developer.apple.com (primary)
  • macrumors.com (primary)
  • techcrunch.com
  • apnews.com

title: ما هي بيئات Docker المعزولة؟ وكيف يعزل Docker وكلاء البرمجة بالذكاء الاصطناعي
description:
ما هي Docker Sandboxes؟ دليل عملي لعزل وكلاء البرمجة بالذكاء الاصطناعي

إجابة سريعة: تشغّل Docker Sandboxes وكلاء البرمجة بالذكاء الاصطناعي مثل Claude Code وCodex وCursor داخل بيئات microVM معزولة، على جهازك أو على سحابة Docker. لكل بيئة معزولة نواة خاصة بها، ونظام ملفات، وشبكة، وDocker Engine خاص. وتديرها عبر sbx CLI المجاني، ولا يصل الوكيل إلا إلى المجلدات والنطاقات التي تسمح بها.

جرّب Apidog اليوم

في 19 نوفمبر 2026، أعادت Docker إطلاق علامتها التجارية حول عبارة واحدة: «الحاويات تعزل أحمال العمل. لكن الوكلاء ليسوا أحمال عمل. الوكلاء فاعلون». لا يقول منشور إعادة العلامة التجارية الكثير عن المنتج نفسه. بل يوجّه القراء إلى Docker Sandboxes وDocker AI Governance، لذا يستخلص هذا الدليل الحقائق من وثائق Docker بدلاً من ذلك.

ما هي Docker Sandboxes؟

Docker Sandboxes هي بيئات microVM معزولة صُممت لتشغيل وكلاء برمجة بالذكاء الاصطناعي يعملون بشكل مستقل. تحصل كل بيئة معزولة على نواة خاصة بها، وDocker daemon، ونظام ملفات وشبكة. داخلها، يتمتع الوكيل بصلاحيات كاملة، بما في ذلك sudo. أما خارجها، فلا يرى سوى مساحة العمل التي تشاركها ووجهات الشبكة التي تسمح بها سياستك.

تدير البيئات المعزولة باستخدام sbx CLI، التي لا تحتاج إلى Docker Desktop أو Docker Engine. وتشغّل الأداة نفسها البيئات المعزولة المحلية على حاسوبك والبيئات المعزولة السحابية على حوسبة تديرها Docker، كما ينقل sbx move نظام ملفات بيئة معزولة بين الاثنين.

تقارن صفحة البنية المعمارية لدى Docker هذا النهج بالبدائل المعتادة:

النهج العزل الوصول إلى Docker الأنسب لـ
Docker Sandboxes (microVMs) كامل (hypervisor) daemon معزول وكلاء مستقلون
حاوية مع تركيب socket جزئي (namespaces) daemon مضيف مشترك أدوات موثوقة
Docker-in-Docker جزئي (privileged) daemon متداخل خطوط أنابيب CI/CD
تنفيذ على المضيف لا يوجد daemon المضيف تطوير يدوي

المقايضة هنا هي موارد مقابل أمان: كل بيئة معزولة تشغّل جهازًا افتراضيًا إضافةً إلى daemon خاص بها، كما أن البيئات المعزولة لا تشارك الصور.

كيف تعزل Docker Sandboxes وكيل الذكاء الاصطناعي؟

تُعد microVM حدود الثقة الرئيسية. ويسرد نموذج الأمان لدى Docker خمس طبقات:

  1. عزل hypervisor. لكل بيئة معزولة نواة منفصلة، دون ذاكرة أو عمليات مشتركة مع المضيف.
  2. عزل الشبكة. يمر TCP الصادر عبر proxy على مضيفك وفق سياسة الرفض افتراضيًا. ويُحظر UDP وICMP افتراضيًا.
  3. عزل Docker Engine. تعمل حاويات الوكيل على محرك خاص دون أي مسار إلى daemon المضيف.
  4. عزل مساحة العمل. أنت تختار ما يراه الوكيل: لا شيء، أو مستودع للقراءة فقط مع نسخة خاصة، أو شجرة عملك بصلاحية القراءة والكتابة.
  5. عزل بيانات الاعتماد. لا تدخل مفاتيح API إلى الجهاز الافتراضي أبدًا. يرى الوكيل قيمة حارسة (sentinel)، ويستبدل proxy المضيف بها بيانات الاعتماد الحقيقية بعد خروج الطلب من البيئة المعزولة.

لا يستطيع وكيل تعرّض لهجوم حقن الموجّه طباعة مفتاح لم يمتلكه قط. لكنه قد يظل قادرًا على استخدام ذلك المفتاح عبر طلبات مسموح بها، لذا فإن سياسة الشبكة لا تقل أهمية عن حيلة بيانات الاعتماد.

توضح Docker أيضًا ما لا يغطيه العزل. في الوضع المباشر، يعدّل الوكيل ملفاتك الحقيقية، بما في ذلك Git hooks، وإعدادات CI، وسكربتات package.json التي تعمل لاحقًا على مضيفك. لا تظهر Git hooks في git diff، لذا تحقق منها بشكل منفصل.

ما الوكلاء الذين تدعمهم Docker Sandboxes؟

تسرد صفحة الوكلاء هؤلاء للبيئات المعزولة المحلية:

  • Claude Code
  • Codex
  • Copilot
  • Cursor
  • Devin
  • Docker Agent
  • Droid
  • Kiro
  • OpenCode
  • Shell، بيئة معزولة بلا وكيل للإعداد اليدوي

يبدأ كل وكيل من صورة قالب. يستخدم Codex الصورة docker/sandbox-templates:codex، وأمر التشغيل الافتراضي لديه هو codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox. منطق Docker: أن microVM وسياسة الشبكة وعزل بيانات الاعتماد تتعامل بالفعل مع ما تحمي منه مطالبات الموافقة. ويمكنك إعادة تفعيل الموافقات داخل الجلسة.

هناك تفصيل في الإعداد يفاجئ الكثيرين. لا تستورد البيئات المعزولة إعدادات على مستوى المستخدم مثل ~/.claude أو ~/.codex، بل فقط إعدادات على مستوى المشروع في دليل العمل.

كيف تُعدّ Docker Sandboxes؟

تحتاج البيئات المعزولة المحلية إلى أحد هؤلاء المضيفين، وفق دليل التثبيت:

نظام التشغيل المتطلبات أمر التثبيت
macOS Sonoma 14 أو أحدث، وApple silicon brew trust docker/tap && brew install docker/tap/sbx
Windows Windows 11، بمعمارية Intel أو AMD 64 بت، وWindows Hypervisor Platform مفعّلة winget install -h Docker.sbx
Linux Ubuntu 24.04 أو أحدث، وKVM مفعّل، والمستخدم عضو في مجموعة kvm سكربت Docker للتثبيت السريع مع SBX=1 (أدناه)

على Ubuntu، يكون الأمر curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sudo SBX=1 sh. ثم اتبع دليل البدء:

  1. سجّل الدخول باستخدام sbx login. تربط Docker كل بيئة معزولة بهوية Docker موثّقة.
  2. خزّن بيانات الاعتماد على المضيف. بالنسبة إلى Codex، يشغّل sbx secret set openai --oauth تدفق OAuth في متصفحك ويحتفظ بالرموز في سلسلة مفاتيح نظام التشغيل.
  3. اختر إعدادًا شبكيًا مسبقًا. يسمح sbx policy init balanced بحركة التطوير المعتادة، بما في ذلك خدمات الذكاء الاصطناعي وسجلات الحزم. الخياران الآخران هما deny-all وallow-all.
  4. شغّل وكيلاً من مجلد مشروعك: 
cd ~/my-project
sbx run --name my-sandbox claude   # or: sbx run codex
  1. راقبه. يعرض sbx ls وكيل كل بيئة معزولة وحالتها ومساحة عملها. ويؤدي الأمر المجرد sbx إلى فتح لوحة معلومات مباشرة.
  2. نظّف. يبقي sbx stop my-sandbox الحزم والصور للاستخدام التالي. بينما يحذف sbx rm my-sandbox كل شيء داخلها؛ وتبقى شجرة العمل على مضيفك كما هي.

سياسة الشبكة ونظام الملفات

تحدد سياسة الشبكة إلى أين يمكن للوكيل أن يذهب. اعرض القواعد، ثم افتح فقط ما تحتاجه المهمة:

sbx policy ls
sbx policy allow network registry.npmjs.org
sbx policy check network api.anthropic.com

يجيب sbx policy check بـ Allowed أو Denied من السياسة النشطة، حتى تتمكن من تأكيد حد قبل أن يبدأ الوكيل. وتحذّر Docker من أن قائمة السماح الافتراضية تتضمن أحرف بدل واسعة مثل *.googleapis.com. احذف ما لا تحتاجه.

يُضبط تعريض نظام الملفات عند إنشاء البيئة المعزولة:

  • التركيب المباشر (الافتراضي في sbx run): يظهر مجلد مشروعك على المسار المطلق نفسه، بصلاحية القراءة والكتابة.
  • وضع الاستنساخ (--clone): يُركّب مستودعك للقراءة فقط، ويعمل الوكيل على نسخة خاصة. مناسب لعدة وكلاء على مستودع واحد.
  • بدون تركيب (sbx create دون مسار): لا تتم مشاركة أي شيء من مضيفك.

لإعدادات فريق قابلة للتكرار، تجمع حزمة (kit) أدوات الوكيل وبيانات اعتماده وقواعد شبكته وإعداده في ملف YAML واحد.

تسعير Docker Sandboxes

تقول الأسئلة الشائعة لدى Docker إن sbx CLI والحوسبة المحلية للبيئات المعزولة مجانية، بما في ذلك للعمل التجاري. أما رسوم مزوّد النموذج فهي منفصلة.

تحتاج البيئات المعزولة السحابية إلى اشتراك Docker Agentic Platform وتُحتسب بالثانية. وسردت صفحة منتج Docker Sandboxes هذه الأسعار في 20 نوفمبر 2026:

الحجم vCPUs الذاكرة لكل ساعة
Micro 1 2 GB $0.07
Small 2 4 GB $0.14
Medium 4 8 GB $0.28
Large 8 16 GB $0.56
XL 16 32 GB $1.12

تنتهي صلاحية البيئات المعزولة السحابية بعد ساعة واحدة افتراضيًا ولا يمكنها تركيب مجلد مضيف. أما حوكمة المؤسسة فهي اشتراك مدفوع منفصل يُباع عبر Docker Sales.

Docker AI Governance وبوابة MCP Enterprise Gateway

Docker AI Governance هي طبقة الفريق فوق البيئات المعزولة. ويقسّمها منشور Docker في 18 نوفمبر إلى ثلاثة أجزاء:

  • سياسات البيئات المعزولة: السماح بالنطاقات ونطاقات IP والمنافذ أو حظرها، والتحكم في مسارات المضيف التي يمكن تركيبها. يتم التنفيذ عند طبقتي proxy والتركيب، لا داخل الوكيل.
  • حوكمة أدوات MCP: يقرر المسؤولون أي خوادم MCP يمكن تسجيلها وأي استدعاءات أدوات يمكن للوكلاء إجراؤها. تُكتب السياسات بلغة Cedar، وتُرفض الطلبات الخاضعة للحوكمة ما لم تسمح بها سياسة.
  • التدقيق والرؤية: سجل لكل قرار سياسة (الجهة الفاعلة، الإجراء، الهدف، القرار، الوقت) يمكن تغذيته إلى SIEM. تحتوي السجلات على بيانات وصفية، لا على الموجّهات.

إليك مثال Cedar من ذلك المنشور، الذي يسمح باستدعاءات أدوات للقراءة فقط على خادم واحد:

permit (principal, action == MCP::Action::"invokeTool", resource)
when {
  resource in MCP::Server::"example" &&
  resource.readOnly == true
};

عند تفعيل حوكمة المؤسسة، تتوقف قواعد السماح المحلية في sbx policy عن السريان؛ بينما تظل قواعد الرفض المحلية مطبقة.

تأتي مكوّنات MCP على مستويين. لكل بيئة معزولة بوابة MCP محلية: سجّل خادمًا مرة واحدة باستخدام sbx mcp add notion --url https://mcp.notion.com/mcp، ثم اعرضه على بيئة معزولة واحدة باستخدام --static-mcp notion. تعمل خوادم stdio المحلية على المضيف، لا داخل الجهاز الافتراضي، لذا تعامل معها كتعليمات برمجية موثوقة على المضيف. وللمؤسسات، تبيع Docker بوابة MCP Enterprise Gateway، التي توافق على الخوادم وتحدد نطاق الأدوات للمجموعات وتسجل كل استدعاء.

حد واحد يجب تذكره: الوكيل الذي يستدعي خادم MCP بعيدًا مباشرة من داخل بيئة معزولة يخضع لسياسة الشبكة، لا لسياسة MCP.

اختبر API من داخل Docker Sandbox باستخدام Apidog CLI

تتيح البيئة المعزولة لوكيلك تغيير التعليمات البرمجية دون تعريض حاسوبك للخطر. لكنه لا يزال بحاجة إلى إثبات أن التغيير يعمل مع API حقيقية. يمنحه Apidog CLI أوامر لحالات الاختبار والتشغيلات، مع إخراج JSON يمكنه قراءته.

تحقق من أن البيئة المعزولة يمكنها الوصول إلى Apidog وAPI الخاصة بك، واسمح لهما إذا رُفضا:

sbx policy check network api.apidog.com
sbx policy allow network api.apidog.com
sbx policy allow network api.example.com

ثم ثبّت وسجّل الدخول داخل البيئة المعزولة:

sbx exec -it my-sandbox bash
npm install -g apidog-cli@latest
apidog auth login --with-token <YOUR_TOKEN>
apidog skill install

Apidog ليس أحد الخدمات التي يحقنها sbx secret set، لذا يعيش هذا الرمز داخل الجهاز الافتراضي. استخدم رمزًا يمكنك إلغاؤه، ونفّذ sbx rm على البيئة المعزولة عند الانتهاء.

أعطِ وكيلك موجّهًا واحدًا:

Using Apidog CLI, create a test case in project <projectId> for
POST /orders on endpoint <endpointId> that asserts a 201 status and an
"id" field in the body. Run it against environment <envId> and
summarize any failures.

يقرأ الوكيل مخطط الحمولة (payload schema)، ويتحقق من ملفه، ويشغّل الحالة:

apidog cli-schema get test-case-create
apidog cli-schema validate test-case-create --file case.json
apidog test-case create --project <projectId> --file case.json
apidog test-case run --project <projectId> --endpoint <endpointId> -e <envId> -r cli,json

خطأ الشبكة عادة يعني أن قائمة السماح أغفلت مضيفًا: أي أن البيئة المعزولة تؤدي عملها. لإعداد خاص بكل وكيل، راجع Apidog CLI داخل Claude Code أو Apidog CLI داخل Codex، واستبدل -r cli,json بـ -r junit في خط أنابيب CI. وتغطي خطة Apidog المجانية حتى 4 مستخدمين.

هل تفضل إبقاء Codex على مضيفك؟ يغطي دليلنا إلى بيئة Codex المعزولة هذا المسار، كما أن CubeSandbox خيار عزل آخر مصمم للوكلاء.

الأسئلة الشائعة

هل Docker Sandboxes مجرد حاويات؟ لا. إنها أجهزة microVM افتراضية بنواة منفصلة لكل بيئة معزولة. تشغّل كل واحدة Docker Engine الخاص بها، لذا يمكن للوكيل بناء حاويات دون لمس daemon المضيف.

هل Docker Sandboxes مجانية؟ sbx CLI والحوسبة المحلية مجانيان، بما في ذلك للعمل التجاري. تبدأ البيئات المعزولة السحابية من $0.07 في الساعة، ورسوم النموذج منفصلة، وحوكمة المؤسسة تكلف إضافية.

هل أحتاج إلى Docker Desktop؟ لا. يُثبّت sbx CLI بمفرده عبر Homebrew أو WinGet أو حزم Ubuntu من Docker.

هل يمكن للوكيل رؤية مفاتيح API الخاصة بي؟ ليس بالنسبة إلى الخدمات التي تديرها sbx، مثل OpenAI وAnthropic وGitHub. يحقن proxy المضيف بيانات الاعتماد تلك، ولا تدخل القيم الخام إلى الجهاز الافتراضي أبدًا. أما أي شيء تثبّته أنت داخل البيئة المعزولة فيعيش هناك بالفعل.

لماذا يعمل Codex دون موافقات داخل بيئة معزولة؟ يبدأ sbx run codex الأمر codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox افتراضيًا، لأن microVM هي حد الأمان. يمكنك إعادة تفعيل مطالبات الموافقة داخل الجلسة.
